newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - AXA-UAP enlarges Sun Life.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - AXA-UAP enlarges Sun Life.

text.p: Sun Life became Britain's third-largest life insurance company on Wednesday after its French owner, the financial giant AXA-UAP group, restructured some of its UK holdings.

Analysts said the restructuring, which has been rumoured for months, was to tie up loose ends left by last year's merger between AXA and UAP, which created. the world's second-largest life insurance group.
They said it consolidated AXA-UAP's British interests and gave it a strong base.
"Combining Sun Life and AXA Equity & Law creates a powerful dynamic business at the centre of the financial services market," said Sun Life chairman Lord Douro.
"The enlarged group will be able to build on both companies' leading positions in a number of key markets and proven track records."

Sun Life & Provincial, which before the transactions was 60.2 percent owned by AXA-UAP, has bought life insurance business AXA Equity & Law and AEL Investment Managers for a total of 690 million pounds ($1.1 billion), as well as AXA's British general insurance business AXA Insurance for 70 million pounds.
Sun Life will issue a total of 247.6 million new shares to AXA-UAP in payment, as well as one third of the enlarged share capital of Sun Life Asset Management.
AXA-UAP will end up owning 72.4 percent of Sun Life but has agreed to vote only a 65 percent share, and will cut its holding to that level by selling shares over an agreed timetable ending in 2000.

Sun Life said the deal would leave it with around 31 billion pounds under management, enhance its earnings from next year and produce cost savings of over 37 million pounds and one-off costs of 48 million pounds over three years.
These savings will be added to those due from cost-saving programmes already in place at both firms.
AXA merged with UAP at the end of last year and had total revenues of around 42.6 billion pounds last year and a market value of around 12.5 billion.
"This deal maximises the opportunities presented by the (AXA-UAP) merger," Sun Life chief executive Mark Wood told Reuters in an interview.
UAP's 60.2 stake in Sun Life which passed to the merged group after the British insurer was floated on the London stock exchange in June last year.

Shares in both Sun Life and AXA-UAP were firmer after the announcement with Sun Life gaining 14 pence to 320 pence but AXA-UAP, after reaching a high of 374.90 francs, later fell back to trade 0.59 percent lower at 367.80 francs at 1030 GMT.
Sun Life said Wednesday's deal would mean the enlarged group will get 84 percent of its income from its life assurance and pensions business.

This will trade as Sun Life in the independent financial adviser (IFA) market and AXA in direct distribution. A new company, Newco, will write the new life business using the resources of AXA's long-term business fund and will be capitalised at 140 million pounds.

In terms of fund management, the enlarged firm will be in the top five life insurance company fund managers, its 31 billion pounds under management comparing to market leader Prudential Corp, Britain's biggest life insurer, which has over 90 billion pounds.
Wood declined to comment on Sun's recent performance but said AXA Equity & Law had had a record quarter for new business in the second three months of the year.
"The market is certainly improving but we're also gaining market share quite strongly as a result of some pretty strong product innovation and some very effective sales management," Wood added.
($ = 0.602 British Pounds)
